Name: Thomas Clarkson
Summary: English abolitionist who gathered first-hand evidence of the slave trade, campaigned for fifty years, and worked alongside Wilberforce in Parliament while mobilising public opinion outside it.
Contribution: Supplied the abolition movement with its evidence, organising testimony and research that made the slave trade's horrors undeniable in Parliament.
KeyWorks: The History of the Rise, Progress, and Accomplishment of the Abolition of the African Slave-Trade
Testimony: He testified that Christian conviction demanded facts as well as feeling, and spent a lifetime collecting them.
